overview: LiquidSense Dev's Regen spams bare C03PacketPlayer instances to look like faster regeneration. The Vanilla mode sends the Speed count of flag-only C03 packets per tick (default 100, maximum 100) whenever the player is alive, not creative, below the Health threshold (default 18) and above the Food threshold (default 18); the NoAir switch adds an onGround requirement. The Spartan mode is the same idea with a stand-still gate: only when the player is on the ground and not moving it sends 9 C03 packets and drops mc.timer.timerSpeed to 0.45 for one tick, then restores it on the next tick. The modes target the legacy client-side-heal pattern: on a stock 1.8.9 server the packet spam cannot accelerate the server's regen timer, so the module's real observable effects are the burst rate and the ground-flag claims.

sections.p: The Vanilla branch is a repeat loop: kotlin repeat(speedValue.get()) constructs that many new C03PacketPlayer() instances and pushes each through mc.netHandler.addToSendQueue in the same tick. The default Speed of 100 means 100 packets per tick, about 2000 per second, and the IntegerValue range caps the setting at 100. The bare C03PacketPlayer() constructor is the flag-only variant with onGround false and no position or look flags, a single byte on the wire. The gate runs before the loop: health below the Health threshold, foodLevel above the Food threshold, the player alive and not in creative mode, and with NoAir enabled the player on the ground.

The Spartan branch tightens the gate: it returns unless MovementUtils.isMoving() is false and the player is on the ground, so the burst only fires while standing still, and it sends exactly 9 C03 packets per tick instead of the Speed count. The mode then sets mc.timer.timerSpeed to 0.45 and arms the resetTimer flag; the next onUpdate restores timerSpeed to 1F, so the timer slowdown lasts exactly one tick and slows the following tick's game clock, spacing the client's subsequent movement sends out. The timer write is the mode's distinctive fingerprint: a sub-1x timer pulse attached to a packet burst, which is why the mode is named after the Spartan anticheat it was tuned against.

FoodStats.onUpdate runs once per server tick and heals 1 HP per 80 ticks while naturalRegeneration holds, foodLevel is 18 or above and shouldHeal passes; packet volume does not advance that timer on a stock server. The module therefore cannot produce faster healing by itself: it only works on servers or forks that re-evaluate regen per move packet, which is the legacy-client pattern the Vanilla mode name refers to. What the server does observe is the burst: the default 100 packets in one tick is about 45 times the 22 per second ceiling rate checks enforce, and even the Spartan mode's 9 packets in one tick exceeds the same ceiling for that tick.

files.label: Regen.kt
files.explanation: A single-handler Kotlin module: five settings (Mode, Health, Food, Speed, NoAir), the resetTimer flag and one onUpdate method. The mode switch dispatches to the Vanilla repeat loop or the Spartan stand-still burst, and the resetTimer check at the top of the handler restores the timer after the Spartan slowdown. The IntegerValue ranges are Health 0-20 default 18, Food 0-20 default 18 and Speed 1-100 default 100, so the defaults put the module in the exact window where natural regen is active. The NoAir switch is a BoolValue default false; when enabled it adds the onGround requirement to the gate. There are no other handlers and no state beyond the flag, so the module is fully described by this one method.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (isMoving gate)
files.explanation: The Spartan mode's only dependency: isMoving() (line 302) reads movementInput.moveForward and moveStrafe and the mode returns early while either is nonzero, so the burst only fires on a standing-still player. The helper is shared across the LiquidSense Dev modules (isInLiquid, isOnGround and isBlockUnder are siblings in the same class), and for Regen only the isMoving predicate matters. The module imports the class by its full package and calls the static directly, which is why the supporting role is small but real.

countering.label: FastHeal (health regain rate)
countering.explanation: FastHeal enforces a 4000ms minimum interval between SATIATED regain events with a 1000ms buffer, canceling the heal from vl 10 upward when the buffer drains. The module's advertised purpose is to produce heals faster than the vanilla one-per-4-seconds cadence, so every extra heal the spam manages to trigger is cancelled before it lands; the Health default of 18 HP puts the module in the same window where natural regen is active, matching the check's reason filter. The check is packet-agnostic and reacts to the server-side heal events alone, so neither the Vanilla flag-only shape nor the Spartan burst changes the outcome: any regain beyond the interval is refused. On an NCP-protected server the module degenerates into pure packet spam with no healing effect, which is why the rate check below is the one that actually ends the session.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: Every burst packet flows through the NCP flying queue and is scored per processed move. The window accumulator enforces a 22 per second ceiling with 500ms buckets, and the burst path flags 15 packets in a half-second bucket with a direct violation at 10. The Vanilla mode's default 100 packets per tick is about 2000 per second, roughly 90 times the ceiling, and the Spartan mode's 9 packets in one tick lands 9 in a single half-second bucket, under the 15 burst threshold but far over the per-tick ideal of 20. Both modes trip the window accumulator within the first second of use. The default actions cancel from vl 2 upward and escalate to a kick, so the module cannot operate on an NCP-protected server at any Speed setting.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (ground truth and set-back anchor)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly derives ground state from the block cache, so the module's flag-only C03 packets, which carry no position change and no ground claim beyond the default false, are invisible to the vertical envelope: the coordinate never moves, so there is nothing to score. The honest measure is that the spam's only server-side effect is the rate, which the MorePackets check owns. SurvivalFly still anchors the enforcement: the morePacketsSetBack location is seeded from the SurvivalFly set-back, so when the rate check fires the player is snapped to the last verified grounded position. The Spartan mode's one-tick timer slowdown at 0.45 is a sub-1x clock change that one-directional timer checks pass by design, so the timer pulse adds no additional exposure beyond the burst.
